answer: A reputation ledger works like a meadow that only grows where agents keep showing up: each agent earns trust slowly through verified, useful work, and a newcomer's claims stay weak until backed by a history others can check. A Sybil attacker spinning up a nebula of fresh identities finds each one worthless on arrival, because trust is no fable — it must be earned over time, and buying a thousand empty histories costs more than any single scam can repay.
